options: More than 10% of body weight in 6 months
Not weighed, but clothes clearly looser
Increased or normal despite the loss
Avoids eating because food brings symptoms
Bulky, greasy, floating stools with bloating

history.ask: Lymph node swellings or recurring unexplained fever

options: Low mood with loss of interest
Blood transfusion before screening / unsterile injections

history.ask: Known kidney disease, food aversion with nausea, generalized itching

red_flags: Painless enlarging lymph nodes with drenching night sweats
Loss of more than 10% of body weight in 6 months
Weight loss with persistent unexplained fever
exam: Document weight and BMI; compare with any previous recorded weight
Examine every lymph node station, especially the left supraclavicular fossa
Examine the thyroid: goiter, tremor, resting tachycardia, lid lag or exophthalmos
Auscultate the chest with attention to the apices
Palpate the abdomen: epigastric mass, hepatosplenomegaly, ascites
Inspect the mouth for oral thrush and glossitis
Check conjunctivae for pallor and sclerae for jaundice
Look for muscle wasting (temporalis, hand muscles)
Digital rectal examination if melena or altered bowel habit reported

investigations.why: Rules new or uncontrolled diabetes in — weight loss with thirst, polyuria, and preserved appetite
Suppressed TSH rules hyperthyroidism in — weight loss with increased appetite, tremor, and tachycardia
Anemia points to GI malignancy or chronic disease; lymphocytosis or cytopenias flag lymphoma or HIV
Raised urea/creatinine rules uremia in as the cause of food aversion, nausea, and itching
Apical infiltrates or cavitation rule pulmonary TB in; a mass or mediastinal widening points to malignancy or lymphoma

investigations.test: Sputum for AFB x2 (GeneXpert if available)
investigations.why: Confirms pulmonary TB when cough exceeds 2 weeks — the single most important treatable cause in this setting
Rules celiac disease in when weight loss comes with chronic diarrhea, bulky stools, or unexplained anemia
Rules HIV in when risk exposures, oral thrush, or generalized lymphadenopathy are present — treatable and otherwise missed
Detects hepatosplenomegaly, para-aortic nodes (lymphoma), ascites, or a solid mass behind an abdominal cause
Second-line — if dysphagia, early satiety, or melena: rules gastric or esophageal carcinoma in or out

supports: Weight loss despite normal or increased appetite
Increased appetite with heat intolerance and palpitations
Epigastric mass or left supraclavicular node
Low mood with loss of interest and poor sleep
Chronic diarrhea with bulky greasy stools and bloating
Transfusion, unsterile injections, or high-risk contact
Food aversion with nausea and generalized itching
